title: regional-graceful-pause-with-proactive-retry-backoff
author: Maya Chen
description: Motivation: During a recent regional degradation incident we observed noisy retries from client SDKs and long-lived stale circuit states preventing safe resume in the router. This PR introduces a regional 'graceful pause' mechanism (soft pause) for low-priority tenant routes and a coordinated proactive retry-backoff in the client-facing retry policy to reduce surge on recovery. The goal is to protect high-priority SLAs while allowing automated, observable, and safe resumption of traffic. Summary of changes: 1) region pause controller that marks a region as soft-paused and applies a per-tenant routing weight delta rather than hard-eviction; 2) adaptive auto-resume policy with hysteresis and observed-healthy-window; 3) client retry policy augmentation: exponential backoff with linear-increase window and jitter tied to region pause TTL; 4) instrumentation and new metrics: region_pause_state, region_pause_decisions, pause_inflight_retries, resume_attempts; 5) safe hotfix for a race in controller resume path that could leave a stale paused flag; 6) operator docs and runbook + integration tests. Implementation notes: the controller runs on the control-plane leader and uses the existing circuit-state store (with a new sticky-epoch tag) to make pause decisions. Pause decisions are governed by SLO thresholds (latency and error budget burn) and configurable tenant priority. Auto-resume will only proceed after three consecutive healthy probes spaced by the probe_interval (configurable), with a backoff if resume attempts fail. The client library change is backward compatible: servers will advertise pause TTL in responses, clients with the new SDK will use it to stretch backoff windows. Backwards compatibility: region pauses are additive and default to disabled; no customer-visible change unless opt-in via operator config or SDK upgrade. Rollout plan: canary on one region for 48h with manual monitor gating, then 25% region rollout, then global. Checklist: - [x] Design review (ENG-2109) - [x] Implementation - [x] Unit + integration tests - [x] Docs + runbook - [x] Canary plan - [x] Hotfix for resume race included - [x] Observability dashboards updated

release_notes:
- Added regional graceful pause controller to protect high-priority SLAs during regional degradation.
- SDK opt-in retry-backoff tied to pause TTL to reduce retry storms on recovery.
- Auto-resume policy with hysteresis and safe guards; includes hotfix for resume race.
- New metrics and dashboard for pause/resume observability.
notes: Canary plan: enable in eu-west-1 for low-traffic tenant subset (prio <= 50) for 48h. Monitor region_pause_state, pause_inflight_retries, retry_delay_histogram, and p99 latency for high-priority tenants. If resume attempts fail twice, system will escalate to SRE and automatically extend pause TTL.
incident_reference: Related to SUP-482 (customer-facing elevated latency in eu-west-1 during 2026-01-29).
testing_summary: Unit tests cover controller state transitions and resume guards. Integration test simulates region degrade and verifies reduced retries and safe resume. Load test script included for canary simulation.
upgrade_instructions: Operator: enable region pause via charts/values/region-pause.yaml (default disabled). SDK: clients should upgrade to the next SDK release to benefit from pause-aware backoff; behavior is backward compatible.
qa_notes: QA verified pause/resume flows and confirmed no disruption for tenants with 'no-degrade' flag. Observability dashboard shows expected retry-delay distribution during simulated recovery.
authors_notes: This PR intentionally keeps pause default off; the control plane only triggers pause when SLO burn is above configured thresholds. We chose soft-weight adjustments to avoid tenant-wide evictions and to keep KV cache warm as much as possible.
